device.name: Lake Shore 336 temperature controller (epics-device-lib ls336 DeviceConnection)

facts.text: The README identifies instruments/ls336.py as the Lake Shore Model 336 temperature controller
The README lists the ls336 driver as a Telnet (RS-232) device exposing temperature/heater inputs and setpoint/PID outputs
The README's inheritance tree lists the repository's other device modules, among them the Rigol DP832 power supply (dp832.py) and the Zaber ASCII motor controller (zaber_motor.py)

For each configured channel whose name does not contain _TI, the Device class creates _TI, _Heater, _Manual, _kP, _kI, _kD, _SP, _Mode and _Range PVs, the _Mode and _Range PVs as mbbOut records built from mode_list and range_list; a _TI channel gets only its temperature PV
Device._create_connection passes settings['ip'], settings['port'] and settings['timeout'] to DeviceConnection
do_sets passes a _Mode PV's new value to set_outmode(chan, new_value, chan, 0), the channel as first and third argument, and a _Range PV's new value to set_range(chan, new_value)
The output-mode menu names Off, Closed Loop, Zone and Open Loop in that order
The heater-range menu names Off, Low, Med and High in that order
do_reads sets channel i's temperature PV from temps[i] and, for a channel without _TI in its name, reads heater, PID, output mode, range, setpoint and manual output for channel i+1
read_temps sends KRDG? 0 and parses four comma-separated floats; the comment calls KRDG a Kelvin reading

The set_pid and read_pid docstrings name channel 1 or 2; set_pid sends PID ,

,, and then PID?, and read_pid sends PID? without its channel argument
read_heater sends HTR? <channel> and read_man_heater sends MOUT? <channel>
The manual-heater docstrings name output percentages, and set_man_heater sends MOUT <channel>,<value> then MOUT? <channel>
set_outmode sends OUTMODE <channel>,<mode>,<in_channel>,<powerup_on> and then OUTMODE? <channel> and returns the first number of the reply; read_outmode sends OUTMODE? <channel>
set_range sends RANGE <channel>,<range> and reads RANGE? <channel> back
set_setpoint sends SETP <channel>,<value> and reads SETP? <channel> back; read_setpoint sends SETP?

Each method from read_temps to read_setpoint reads one line with read_until(b'\n', timeout=2), parses it with a regex search and, on any Exception (a reply the regex does not match included), prints the error and raises OSError
TelnetConnection's constructor stores host, port and timeout and creates a TelnetSocket to host:port as self.tn; an exception from that is printed, not raised
TelnetSocket.read_until returns whatever has arrived when the timeout or EOF comes instead of raising

safe_state.description: the configured heater output is in output mode Off, confirmed by an OUTMODE? readback of mode 0; the stop command (OUTMODE <channel>,0,<channel>,0) also sets that output's control input to input <channel> and its powerup enable to 0; its heater range, setpoint and manual output are kept, the other heater output is not commanded and keeps heating if it was on, and nothing cools the sample
